_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The Scout Energy Management LLC (Scout), Ashley Compressor Station (ACS) is a natural agas compressor station located approximately 12 miles southwest of Myton, Duchesne County, Utah within the Greater Monument Butte Oil and Gas Unit.  The facility consists of separation and dehydration operations, production liquids storage and transfer operations, compression operations, and natural gas liquids (NGL) extraction, storage, and transfer operations.   

It is Scout's policy to adhere to all applicable federal, state, and local laws. The purpose of this Risk Management Plan is to provide information about operations at the facility, programs to prevent accidental chemical releases, emergency response plans in the event of an accidental release, the five-year accident history of the facility, and planned changes to improve safety at the facility.

The NGL extraction process is performed utilizing a Joules Thompson skid with the NGL stored within a 18,000-gallon pressure vessel until transferred off site by truck.   The NGL contains EPA/RMP-covered flammable substances including methane, ethane, propane, butane, isobutane, pentane, and isopentane; three of which are in quantities greater than the threshold planning quantity of 10,000 lbs. The ACS does not have any EPA/RMP-regulated toxic chemicals. The facility is regulated under EPA Risk Management Program 40 CFR Part 68 - Program Level 1 requirements.

This facility complies with EPA's accident prevention rule and all applicable state and local codes and regulations.  In the event of a leak or overflow, all valves associated with that portion of the system will be closed and the system shut down to prevent additional releases while response procedures are initiated.  When a spill occurs outside of the containment, or in the event of a large or catastrophic release, personnel must take the necessary precautions to contain the spill to the site.  Immediate notification to designated Scout personnel is mandated and is the

key to effective spill and release containment and control.  Such notification also allows the company to promptly report a spill event to appropriate government agencies, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

Five-year accident history:
The ACS has not had an accident in the last five years that caused onsite or offsite deaths, injuries, property or environmental damage, evacuations, or sheltering in place.

The emergency response program:
Scout maintains a general Emergency Plan for the ACS.  
The facility will continue to coordinate any emergency response actions necessary with the Duchesne County Fire & Emergency Management Office. Scout employees are trained with the expectation that they will evacuate and restrict access to the facility until both the safety and exposure potentials are no longer a threat. All employees are trained to discover releases and take no further action beyond making notification. 

Should a malfunction or minor release occur, the operator on duty should assess the nature and severity of the release, fire or emergency. The operator should take action to stop small releases of flammable materials.  The on-duty Operator or Maintenance personnel working at Scout Compressor Stations, has full authority to activate the emergency shutdown system (ESD) at any time should he feel that a malfunction creates a situation hazardous enough to warrant the emergency shutdown of equipment or evacuation of the facility.  Upon activation of the ESD the operator should evacuate the facility in an orderly manner and proceed to a safe muster location where evaluations and notifications including notification to the Superintendent, Foreman, and Lead can be made.  Normally, the Foreman is responsible for coordinating emergency actions, and essential planning for effectively protecting workers, the public, and the environment during emergency situations.
